characterizations.result_summary: Equilibrium melting temperature of sPP determined to be 150 °C via Hoffman-Weeks analysis of DSC heating scans.

evidence.source_sentence: The thermal crystallization behavior of sPP/PEP blends was analyzed by a PerkinElmer DSC-7 differential scanning calorimeter. First, the samples were heated from room temperature to 200 $^ \circ \mathrm { C }$and annealed for 10 min in the melt. The samples were then quickly quenched to the desired crystallization temperature $( T _ { \mathrm { c } } )$at a cooling rate of 130 °C/min. After complete crystallization, the samples were reheated to a melt with a heating rate of $4 ~ { ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C / m i n } }$.

By extrapolating both lines of $T _ { \mathrm { m 1 , s P P } }$versus $T _ { \mathrm { c } }$and $T _ { \mathrm { m 2 , s P P } }$versus $T _ { \mathrm { c } }$to the line $T _ { \mathrm { m } } \overset { \cdot } { = } T _ { \mathrm { c } } ,$, according to the linear Hoffman–Weeks analysis,<sup>28</sup> we obtain the same value of the equilibrium melting temperature of sPP, $T _ { \mathrm { m , s P P } } ^ { \mathrm { ^ { \circ } } } ,$which is around 150 °C.

characterizations.result_summary: Equilibrium melting temperature of PEP determined to be 189 °C via Hoffman-Weeks analysis of DSC heating scans.

evidence.source_sentence: The thermal crystallization behavior of sPP/PEP blends was analyzed by a PerkinElmer DSC-7 differential scanning calorimeter. First, the samples were heated from room temperature to 200 $^ \circ \mathrm { C }$and annealed for 10 min in the melt. The samples were then quickly quenched to the desired crystallization temperature $( T _ { \mathrm { c } } )$at a cooling rate of 130 °C/min. After complete crystallization, the samples were reheated to a melt with a heating rate of $4 ~ { ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C / m i n } }$.

According to the linear Hoffman–Weeks analysis, the equilibrium melting temperature of PEP, $T _ { \mathrm { m , P E P } } ^ { \mathrm { ^ { \circ } } } ,$is found to be equal to 189 $^ \circ \mathrm { C }$.
